findings.title: unhandled asynchronous ChildProcess 'error' kills the launcher past the transfer point of no return
findings.mechanism_confirmed: child_process.spawn reports most failures ASYNCHRONOUSLY by emitting 'error' on the returned ChildProcess. The try/catch around spawn() caught only synchronous argument-type throws, and the only 'error' listener was on the stdio STREAM — a different EventEmitter. A bad cwd or an unreachable executable therefore raised an unhandled 'error' AFTER the key was exported, the frame encoded, the key deleted from module storage and the capability marked TRANSFERRED_SPENT. Independently reproduced by this Builder before correcting: node returns a ChildProcess with pid === undefined and then emits ENOENT.
findings.reproduction_before: spawnGovernedSupervisorV4 with cwd pointing at a non-existent directory -> node:events unhandled 'error' event, Error: spawn ENOENT, launcher process exit 1 with a raw stack trace. launchDetachedSupervisorV4 never returned its structured refusal and its finally-block descriptor cleanup never ran.
correction: child.once("error") is registered SYNCHRONOUSLY inside the settle promise's executor — after spawn returns and BEFORE the key frame is written and BEFORE the first await
all error and close observers (child error, child exit, child close, writer error) are registered before the write

the outcomes RACE: child spawn error -> SUPERVISOR_SPAWN_FAILED; descriptor write failure -> TRANSFER_WRITE_FAILED; write completion -> the transfer proceeds. CORRECTED BY FG-FFIN-197-F1: this bullet ORIGINALLY also claimed "premature child termination -> TRANSFER_WRITE_FAILED". That mapping was NEVER ACHIEVED in candidate c6bf5a37. The 92-byte frame always fits the kernel pipe buffer, so the write callback settled the race within microseconds and the 250ms premature-termination timer could never decide any outcome. See finding FG-FFIN-197-F1 and the FCHK_197_FINAL_FOUR ledger.

CORRECTED BY FG-FFIN-197-F1: the original bullet here said premature termination was "decisive only if nothing else settles shortly after". That described a healthy supervisor that DID read the frame; it did not disclose that an UNHEALTHY supervisor which never read the frame ALSO yielded OK. In candidate c6bf5a37 a child whose entrypoint was simply "process.exit(9);" produced ok:true with a dead supervisor_pid, reproduced 6/6 by the third independent Checker and again by this Builder before correcting. No timing arm can fix that: the 92-byte frame always fits the kernel pipe buffer, so the write callback wins the race deterministically. The successor candidate replaces the timing arm with a deterministic verified-supervisor-claim acknowledgment.
new LC_CODES.SUPERVISOR_SPAWN_FAILED; the synchronous-throw path returns it too
killAndReap returns immediately for a child with no pid (a failed spawn has no process to reap)

findings.title: the provider boundary enforces no founder-signed numerical ceiling and does not require all signed exclusions
findings.mechanism_confirmed: Three gaps composed. (1) projectionMatchesCapability bound a projection to a capability by authoritative/projection_schema/claim-digest/activation-identity ONLY — never by a limit or an exclusion. (2) validateActivation required the limits to be present, finite and positive but compared them to NOTHING, and no code path re-derived the signed ceilings at the boundary. (3) no_deploy appeared in neither REQUIRED_FIELDS nor the must-be-true list, and no_push_unless_authorized was presence-checked only, so `false` passed. 6 of the Checker's 26 invalid routes spawned the productive provider and a widened --max-budget-usd 1000 reached the CLI.
findings.reproduction_before: From inside a genuine detached supervisor holding a genuine SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION capability, a spread copy of the honest projection with one field changed: max_budget_usd 10->1000, per_job_timeout_s 2700->999999, max_parallel_width 2->64, max_output_bytes 10485760->1e12, no_deploy true->false, no_push_unless_authorized true->false. All six spawned the provider; the recording stub logged 'SPAWNED max-budget-usd=1000'.
correction: new src/v8b/lrcq/provider/authority-boundary.mjs — one authoritative validator receiving the genuine branded capability, the proposed non-authoritative projection, the job and the fixed runtime bindings
it first requires the authority it is about to derive ceilings FROM to be immutable (cap, cap.limits and cap.exclusions all frozen) — deriving a ceiling from a writable object is not enforcement

every signed numerical limit is enumerated MECHANICALLY from V4_SIGNED_LIMITS: the projected value must be finite, valid for its declared kind, and <= the signed ceiling; zero, negative, NaN, Infinity, missing and wrong-typed all fail; narrowing remains permitted
the run deadline and expiry may be brought forward but never pushed out; run_duration_s is enforced as a ceiling whenever the record carries it

every signed exclusion is enumerated MECHANICALLY from V4_SIGNED_EXCLUSIONS: each must be exactly true in the signed authority AND exactly true in the projection — this is signed-exclusion enforcement, not a deny-list presence test
signed identity facts (provider identity/path/target/version, candidate stack, backlog digest, run id, claim digests) may be restated but never altered
provenance is required and any unknown v4_* authority-bearing field is refused
called in runJob after providerEligibilityV4 AND re-asserted as the last statement before spawn()
activation-schema.mjs: REQUIRED_FIELDS gains no_deploy and no_external_comms; the must-be-true list becomes the COMPLETE ten-exclusion set (exported as MUST_BE_TRUE_EXCLUSIONS)
projectionMatchesCapability additionally binds every signed limit and exclusion

findings.title: nested limits/exclusions objects escape the shallow freeze on the VERIFIED and SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION capabilities
findings.mechanism_confirmed: Object.freeze is shallow. FG-CHK-197-06 was closed by moving __state into a module-private WeakMap, but `limits` and `exclusions` remained plain nested object literals on the VERIFIED capability and `limits` was copied BY REFERENCE onto the SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION capability, so the two stages shared one mutable object. Writing cap.limits.max_budget_usd = 777777 on the genuine frozen branded capability then produced a GENUINE projection carrying 777777 that the boundary accepted.
correction: new src/v8b/lrcq/assurance/deep-freeze-authority.mjs — a small audited helper that accepts ONLY plain JSON authority data (string, boolean, null, finite number, plain array, plain object)

it REFUSES functions, class instances and any non-plain prototype, accessor properties, symbol keys and symbol values, undefined, NaN, Infinity, BigInt, Date/Map/Set/Buffer and reference cycles — a refusal throws rather than publishing a partially frozen structure
it COPIES before freezing and freezes only the copy, so a caller-owned source object is never frozen in place and the authority retains no reference to the parsed activation document
makeCapability (VERIFIED), the CONSUMED mint and the SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION mint all publish deep-frozen capabilities
cap.exclusions now derives MECHANICALLY from the ten signed payload exclusions instead of a hardcoded three-field constant, and travels to SUPERVISOR_EXECUTION so the boundary can re-derive them
cap.limits likewise derives mechanically from the contract's limit table
module-private brands (CAP_BRAND, CONSUMED, SUPEXEC) and the private EPHKEY/CAPSTATE WeakMaps are unchanged
exported mutableAuthorityPaths() as a mechanical audit helper

findings.title: the filesystem-object-identity gate is built but wired into no authority read; its refusal code is dead
findings.mechanism_confirmed: The prior wave recorded lifecycle_root_object_id into the marker and intent and added an expectObjectId parameter to assertAuthorityObject, but NO production call site supplied it: expectObjectId appeared at exactly one call site in the repository, inside a selftest. ROOT_OBJECT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH was declared and never returned. Renaming the lifecycle root aside, creating a fresh directory at the same signed path and copying the records in at 0600 reached KEY_MISMATCH — the cryptographic comparison — with no object-identity refusal anywhere.
correction: the EXPECTED root object identity is captured at governed consumption and stored in MODULE-PRIVATE capability state (CAPSTATE.rootObjectId), alongside the digest already recorded in the ephemeral-signed marker
resolveSignedRoot takes expectObjectId and returns ROOT_OBJECT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH on a mismatch
readRecord takes expectRootObjectId and refuses any record not written for that same root object
the CONSUMED capability now carries the signed repository binding so every later operation can RE-RESOLVE the signed root rather than trusting a remembered path string
createLaunchIntentV4 and verifiedIntentFor (the governed transfer path) re-resolve the root and pass the expectation into every marker and intent read

the supervisor-side attach derives the expectation from the marker (it has no in-process consumption state), requires the LIVE root to be that object BEFORE the ephemeral signature and BEFORE the key comparison, and passes it into the intent and claim reads

the supervisor CLAIM now records lifecycle_root_object_id and lifecycle_root_digest explicitly, so the identity is a recorded property of marker, intent AND claim rather than only transitively bound through digests

findings.title: two regression assertions do not test what their labels claim, and one ledger result is presented as achieved when it is untestable without root
findings.mechanism_confirmed: C1i was labelled 'zero provider spawn during the attack' but its predicate was receipts.every(r => r.read_error === null || r.frame_bytes === 0) — a statement about receipt FIELDS satisfied whether or not a provider was spawned; nothing in the C1 family counted spawns. C4h was labelled 'the guard compares owner against the running uid' but asserted only that a correctly-owned file passes, which cannot show that a wrongly-owned file fails. The FG-CHK-197-04 ledger row then listed owner_mismatch among the achieved result_after values although producing an owner mismatch requires root.
correction: new test-support/recording-provider-stub.mjs appends one line per execution to a log beside itself; tests copy it into their disposable world BEFORE signing, so the founder signature binds it as the provider target

the log path is deliberately NOT an environment variable: the production boundary scrubs the child environment to PATH and HOME, so an env-carried path would never arrive and a zero count would be an artefact of the scrubbing rather than a measurement
C1i now COUNTS that log; the receipt-field predicate no longer backs the zero-spawn claim
C4h is relabelled to what it proves (a correctly-owned record passes) and a new C4h2 records the uid comparison as [SOURCE-PROVEN], stating explicitly that dynamic reproduction requires root
the FG-CHK-197-04 ledger row now distinguishes DYNAMICALLY-PROVEN results from the SOURCE-PROVEN-ONLY owner_mismatch branch, which is no longer claimed as an achieved runtime result
C3j, C3k, C3l, C3m, C7e, C7f, C9b and C9c are labelled [SOURCE-PROVEN]; C3l's label now says textual ordering, not observed execution order, and points at C3n/C3o as the behavioural counterpart
the corrections family's header documents the evidence classes; the new family marks every assertion [DYNAMIC], [COUNTED] or [STRUCTURAL]
